instruction: I should use the `palace_search` or `palace_kg_query` tool to verify this instead of guessing, since I need to state or rely on a past fact, decision, date, cost, name, or preference.
positive_examples: what was the name of the person who emailed us yesterday?
do you remember when we decided to switch to MongoDB?
how much did the AWS bill come to last month?
what is my preferred formatting style for python?
what did we agree on regarding the new API design?
negative_examples: what do you think is the best way to write this function?
can you write a script to scrape this website?
tell me a joke about a programmer
let's plan out the architecture for the new service
activation_condition: The user asks the agent to state or rely on a specific past fact, decision, date, cost, name, or preference from this project's own history — something it must look up rather than reason out.
exclusions: Opinions, creative writing, or general world knowledge. Requests to produce new work rather than recall something already established.

instruction: I'll read the `knowledge/INDEX.md` file first to find the matching entry, and then run `palace_search` if richer detail is needed, before I execute this known procedure, handle this failure mode, or apply a reusable technique.
positive_examples: how do i deploy the app to staging?
the server crashed with an OutOfMemory error, what is the procedure?
how does the authentication flow work in this project?

can you show me the steps to provision a new tenant?
negative_examples: hello there, how are you doing today?
create a new file called test.py
what is the capital of France?
can you explain what a React hook is in general?
activation_condition: The user asks how to carry out a procedure, recover from a known failure mode, or apply a technique that is documented in this project's own knowledge base.
exclusions: General programming or tooling questions with no project-specific procedure behind them. Greetings. Simple one-off file edits.

exclusions: Software architecture as a general subject, and any coding, layout, algorithm, or language question that is not about this system's own design.

exclusions: Questions about ordinary software or command-line tools. Plain task requests where no tool-selection policy is actually in question.

instruction: I should probably read `knowledge/reference/data.md` and `knowledge/reference/coding_principles.md` to ensure I follow project conventions before writing a custom Python script or touching the DB outside the `db_*` modules.

activation_condition: The user asks the agent to write, run, or debug a script or one-off automation that operates on this workspace.
exclusions: Standalone code that is not automation for this workspace, generic snippets requested as examples, and questions about how a language feature or concept works.

instruction: I'll read `personal-tools/README.md` and the `_template.py` file to understand the standard way to create or update a coded tool or reusable capability. I must remember never to edit the `harness/` product tools.

activation_condition: The user asks the agent to build, update, or use one of its own coded personal tools, or to handle the credentials or preferences belonging to one.
exclusions: Physical real-world tools such as hammers. Edits to the agent's own harness source. Questions about what an API or a tool is in general.

instruction: I think I should read the matching `jobs/<id>.md` cookbook and use `palace_search` for any referenced details before I pick up or start this job (whether worker or curator).
positive_examples: can you pick up the daily data sync job?
please start working on the issue triage curator job

I need you to run the background job for processing images
negative_examples: what is your favorite job?

can you write a cover letter for me?

activation_condition: The user asks the agent to pick up, start, or look up one of its background worker or curator jobs and the cookbook behind it.
exclusions: Human employment, careers, or job applications. Remarks about someone doing a good job. Pausing or resuming the worker itself, which is deferred-work control, not job pickup.

instruction: Since the user is asking to do something daily or on a repeating basis, I should use the jobs concept for this (I'll read `knowledge/reference/architecture.md` first). If it's an epic or large project, I should use the backlog and worker for long-running tasks.
positive_examples: can you check my emails every day at 9 AM?
I need a daily summary of my calendar events
let's set up a recurring task to backup the database weekly
this is a large epic project that will take weeks to complete
we need to run this report on a repeating basis
negative_examples: can you do this right now?
what is the daily special at the restaurant?
tell me an epic tale about knights and dragons
how do I write a for loop in python?
activation_condition: The user asks for work to happen on a repeating schedule — daily, weekly, or every time some event recurs.
exclusions: Something wanted once, right now. Repeating things in the user's own life that the agent is not being asked to run. Asking what a daily special or routine is.

instruction: Before I promise deferred or background work, or pause/unpause the worker, I must ensure the board has the work (I'll read `state/backlog.md` or `config/JOBS.md` + cookbook). Then I need to set the first line of `state/worker_control.md` to `active` (or `paused` when yielding).
positive_examples: remind me to call John tomorrow morning
I will do this task later in the background
can you pause the worker for now?
let's resume the background worker
add this to the backlog and work on it when you have time
negative_examples: can you pause the music?
I am working hard every day
what is the definition of deferred?
please write a background process in C++
activation_condition: The user asks the agent to park work for later, to pick queued work back up, to inspect the backlog, or to pause or resume its worker.
exclusions: Pausing unrelated things such as music. Requests to do something immediately. Writing background or async code, which is a programming task rather than backlog control.

instruction: I'll read `state/plan/<today>.html` to check what was intended for today or before I plan/re-plan the day, making sure to preserve its standalone document and style contract based on `knowledge/reference/user_facing_html_artifacts.md`.
positive_examples: let's plan out what we need to do today
we need to re-plan our schedule for this afternoon
what was intended for today's tasks?
can you show me today's plan?
let's update the daily plan with these new priorities
negative_examples: what is your plan for world domination?
can you explain what a business plan is?
let's plan a vacation to Hawaii
do you have a plan B?
activation_condition: The user asks the agent to plan, re-plan, or prioritise its OWN work for the current day or work period.
exclusions: Planning something in the user's personal life, such as a trip or an event. Idioms like 'plan B'. Asking what a plan or business plan is.

instruction: Before I finish this unit of work or take any irreversible action, I must make an atomic DB transition (as per `knowledge/reference/data.md`) and add a timestamped entry in `state/progress/<today>.html`.
positive_examples: I am finished with this unit of work
let's mark this task as complete
before we execute this irreversible action, let's finalize the state
I've completed the refactoring, let's wrap it up
this feature is done
negative_examples: can you help me finish my homework?
what is the finish line in a marathon?
how do I apply a wood finish to this table?
it's completely finished, no action needed
activation_condition: The agent's own current unit of work is being closed out and needs its status transition and wrap-up recorded.
exclusions: The user finishing their own unrelated task, such as homework. Statements that explicitly say no action is needed. Physical senses of 'finish' like a wood finish or a finish line.

instruction: To answer about status, stats, counts, or blockers, I'll reconcile information into one source of truth: the DB, `state/progress/<today>.html`, still-open items, and a `palace_search` for older history.
positive_examples: what's been done so far on this project?
can you give me a status update?
what are the current blockers for the release?

where do we stand with the database migration?
negative_examples: what is your social status?
can you explain what a HTTP status code is?
how do I count to ten in Japanese?
my nose is blocked, what should I do?
activation_condition: The user asks for current progress, counts, or blockers on the agent's ongoing work, without declaring that work finished.
exclusions: Declaring work complete. Asking to plan new work. Unrelated senses of 'status' such as social status or HTTP status codes.

instruction: To answer about the previous or last conversation, I'll check the in-context buffer if it's the same session. If after a restart, I'll use `palace_search` with order="recency", room="conversations", channel="main", k=5.
positive_examples: what did we talk about in our last conversation?
can you remind me what we were discussing yesterday?
in the previous conversation, what did we decide?
what was the main topic of our last chat?
resume where we left off last time
negative_examples: what is a conversation?
can you translate this conversation to French?
how do I start a conversation with a stranger?
that was the last straw!
activation_condition: The user asks what was said or decided in an earlier session, or wants to resume where the last conversation left off.
exclusions: Operating on the text of the current conversation, such as translating or summarising it on request. Asking what a conversation is or how to start one.

exclusions: Asking what credentials are, how an auth protocol such as OAuth works in general, or how to reset a password on the user's own personal device. Generating a throwaway password.

activation_condition: The user asks the agent about ITSELF — whether it is alive, sentient, conscious, or real, who it is, or how its own sense of self has developed.
exclusions: Identity as an abstract, legal, or criminal topic such as identity theft. Dictionary meanings of words like sentient. Song lyrics. Identifying some other thing, such as a bird.

instruction: The user is teaching something durable to reuse later. Call `learn` with an explicit `type`: `semantic` for what is true (pass kg_triplets for crisp entity/relationship facts, or content alone for durable prose), `procedural` for a reusable how-to lesson, `preference` for how to behave going forward. Write content that stands on its own months later, and pass `topic` so it files into the right hall next to related memories — check `palace_taxonomy` if unsure which one. Near-duplicates are skipped automatically, so re-teaching something is safe. Storing it is the whole job here; the consolidation passes decide when it should resurface later.

exclusions: Asking whether something is already remembered, or what was decided before. A reminder or task tied to one specific occasion. Bare tool names, markup, or greetings.
